[T3 Code: the agent in T3 thread "c8d8c05a-d815-49e5-8e39-b5a4a31bd45c" sent this message, not the user.]

Act as the implementation sub-agent for this task.

You are working in the Moneo repo (read AGENTS.md first and follow it exactly: no comments, surgical changes, tests only where they catch a real bug, QA backend only — never the owner's backend on port 3000 or `.env`). Your checkout is based on the latest `main`. Create a branch `t3/audit-small-ui`, commit each part separately in plain language, push, and open ONE pull request to `main`. Do not merge it. Do not touch PR #313.

## Three UI fixes from a QA audit (owner chose all three in one PR)

### (a) Add account popover opens off screen at 320 px
`app/money/accounts/page.tsx` (~line 132) renders the form inside `AddAccountPanel` (`app/money/accounts/add-account-panel.tsx`, a `<details>`) with `absolute right-0 … w-72 max-w-[calc(100vw-2rem)]`. At 320×568 the trigger wraps under the heading on the left, so a right-aligned 288 px panel starts 163 px left of the viewport, clipping labels, fields and submit. At 390 px it fits. Make the panel stay fully on screen at any width (e.g. align to the left edge when the trigger is on the left / at small widths, or position it within the viewport) without changing desktop placement. Escape/focus-return already works — keep it. Check whether other `<details>` popovers in the app use the same `absolute right-0` pattern next to a wrapping trigger and fix them the same way if so (fix the class, not just this case) — but keep it surgical.

### (b) Fresh Overview shows an empty Cash flow chart with no message
On a workspace with no transactions, Home/Overview shows a large empty Cash flow chart with its controls and no explanation, which reads as a chart that failed to load. Find the Cash flow widget (search `components/` and `app/` for the cash flow widget used on Home; see `FEATURES.md` for widget names). When there are no transactions in the range because the workspace has no transactions at all, show a short empty state instead of the blank canvas: "Import a statement or connect a bank to see cash flow." with links to `/import` (statement) and the bank section. If there ARE transactions but none in the chosen range, say so instead ("No transactions in this period"). Keep the card's height stable so Home doesn't shift.

### (c) Mobile truncation
On phones (390 px), from audit screenshots with synthetic data:
- Home stacked cards truncate account names and agent role labels to one line.
- A large amount wrapped across multiple lines.
- Mobile Transactions shortens several distinct row descriptions to the same visible prefix.
Fix: names, role labels and transaction descriptions get up to two lines (`line-clamp-2`, with the full text in a `title` attribute) instead of single-line truncation, on mobile widths. Money amounts never wrap: `whitespace-nowrap` + tabular nums, and where the space is too narrow show the compact form (e.g. €1.2M) with the full value in `title`/accessible label. Look for the existing money formatting helper (in `lib/` — e.g. a `formatMoney`/`money` function) and add the compact variant there rather than formatting in components; money is integer minor units with an explicit currency (AGENTS.md). Unit-test the compact formatter (rounding, negative values, a currency with 0 minor digits like JPY) — that is money display logic worth a test.

## Checks
- `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run check:bundle`.
- Skill `verify-ui` on the QA app (`npm run qa:server`; `npm run qa:shots -- <label> home money/accounts money/transactions` — see AGENTS.md; set up QA with `npm run setup -- --qa` / `npm run qa:auth` if needed; seed only synthetic data, including an empty workspace for (b) and a long account name + a large amount for (c)). Before/after at 320×568 for (a), empty Home for (b), 390×844 Home and Transactions for (c), light and dark. Embed them in the PR (pattern: a `pr-assets/<pr>` branch).
- If an existing browser journey (e.g. `e2e/accessibility.gated.spec.ts` "core screens fit mobile") can assert the popover is within the viewport at 320 px, extend it rather than adding a new spec.
- **Speed** section (skill `measure-speed`): Home and Accounts open times before/after.
- End commit messages with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>` and the PR description with `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)`.

When done, your last line must be: PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>.

---
name: verify-ui
description: Prove a Moneo change works by driving the real QA app the way the owner would, and attach the evidence (screenshots in light, dark and mobile, or a recording) to the pull request. Use after any change to a page, component, style or user flow, when asked to "verify", "show me it works" or "add screenshots", and before opening a PR that changes what the owner sees.
---

# Verify a change in the running app

The owner reviews what the app does, not the diff. "It compiles" and "the tests pass" are not proof; pictures and recordings of the real app are.

Everything here runs against the QA app on http://localhost:3100. Never use port 3000; that is the owner's app and data.

## 1. Launch

`npm run setup -- --qa`, then `npm run qa:auth`, then `npm run qa:server` in the background. It is ready when `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "x-moneo-test: 1" http://localhost:3100/api/health` prints 401 or 200.

If port 3100 is already taken, another checkout's QA app owns it and serves that checkout's code. Do not kill it. Start this checkout's app on a free port with `QA_PORT=<port> npm run qa:server` and point the tools at it with `E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:<port>`.

## 2. Doctor

Run this whenever anything looks off, before changing code:

`npm run qa:shots -- doctor home`

It fails with the reason when the app is not worth driving:

- **"The QA session was not accepted"**: the saved session expired (they last an hour). Run `npm run qa:auth`.
- **Every page is the "could not sign you in" screen after a fresh `qa:auth`**: the shared QA workspace holds data this checkout cannot read. Run `npm run qa:reset`.
- **A failed request or console error on an untouched page**: the base is broken. Fix or report that first; evidence taken on a broken base proves nothing.

## 3. Drive

1. **List the pages.** Every route the change can affect, including the ones AGENTS.md "Hit every surface" names. `FEATURES.md` shows a feature's pages, widgets, chat tools and voice routes together.
2. **Set up the state.** If a page needs data, create it the way the nearest spec in `e2e/` does. An empty page proves an empty page.
3. **Before.** With the change set aside (a temporary commit on another branch, or `git worktree add` of the base):
   `npm run qa:shots -- before home money/transactions`
   Name pages without the leading slash (Git Bash rewrites `/paths`); `home` is `/`.
4. **After.** On the changed code, the same command with `after`.

Each run writes `<page>-light.png`, `<page>-dark.png` and `<page>-mobile.png` to `.qa/shots/<label>/`, prints the HTTP status and every failed request or console error per page, and exits 1 if there were any.

**A flow, not a page.** A screenshot cannot show a tap, a card being accepted or an undo. Extend the journey spec in `e2e/` that already covers the flow and record it:

`npx playwright test e2e/<spec> --workers=1 --trace on --video on`

Add a new spec only when no existing journey can take the check (AGENTS.md Tests).

## 4. Evidence

- Use the path the owner uses: real pages, real buttons. Not a test-only endpoint or a direct database write for the step under test.
- Capture the action and the state it leaves, not only the last screen.
- Check the side effects next to what is visible: the row written, the history entry, what undo restores.
- **Look at every picture yourself.** Read each PNG. Check for overflow, clipped text, unreadable contrast in dark and a broken layout on mobile. A console error or a status of 400 or more is a failure: fix it and shoot again.
- When something looks wrong, suspect the capture before the app, and measure the live page before reporting a bug.

## 5. Hand over

The pictures go in the PR description itself, so the owner sees them on GitHub. A path to `.qa/` is not evidence: it is git-ignored and exists only on this machine. Never commit them to the PR's branch either.

1. Open the PR first to get its number.
2. Push the files to their own branch, `pr-assets/<pr>`, which holds nothing else. The repo is public, so QA data only:

   ```sh
   git worktree add --orphan -b pr-assets/<pr> .qa/pr-assets
   cp -r .qa/shots/before .qa/shots/after .qa/pr-assets/
   git -C .qa/pr-assets add -A
   git -C .qa/pr-assets commit -m "Screenshots for #<pr> (QA data)"
   git -C .qa/pr-assets push origin pr-assets/<pr>
   git worktree remove .qa/pr-assets
   ```

   To add more later, check the branch out again with `git worktree add .qa/pr-assets pr-assets/<pr>`.
3. Embed them with `gh pr edit <pr> --body-file <file>`, before and after side by side in a table, one row per page and view that visibly changed, with one line on what to look at:

   ```markdown
   | Before | After |
   | --- | --- |
   | ![Home, dark, before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/indkhan/Moneo/pr-assets/<pr>/before/home-dark.png) | ![Home, dark, after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/indkhan/Moneo/pr-assets/<pr>/after/home-dark.png) |
   ```

4. **A flow:** GitHub plays a GIF inline but not a video from a branch. If `ffmpeg` is installed, turn the recording into a GIF and embed it: `ffmpeg -i video.webm -vf "fps=10,scale=900:-1" flow.gif`. Otherwise embed a screenshot of each key state. Either way, push the recording too (`video.webm` from `test-results/`) and link it.
5. Open the PR on GitHub and check that every image shows.

Say which pages you covered, what changed in each and what you could not capture and why. If nothing visibly changed, say so and attach nothing.

## 6. Clean up

Stop only the server you started, found by its port and this checkout's path, never by name. Leave `.qa/shots/` in place: cleanup removes instances, never the evidence.

name: measure-speed
description: Measure how fast Moneo opens and how fast the changed action runs, before and after a change, and put the numbers in the pull request. Use before opening any PR that changes code, when asked "is it faster", "measure speed" or "check performance", and when a change could slow a page, an import, a sync, a chat answer or start-up.
---

# Measure speed before and after

Every change should leave Moneo as fast as before or faster. Measure it; never guess. A PR that only changes docs (`*.md`, `docs/`) skips this and writes "No runtime change" under Speed.

Everything runs against the QA backend, never port 3000, on production builds: `next dev` compiles each page on its first visit and makes everything look slow.

## 1. Two builds

- **After:** this checkout. `QA_PORT=3101 npm run qa:server -- --production` in the background.
- **Before:** the PR's base in its own worktree: `git worktree add ../moneo-speed-base origin/main`, then in it `npm ci`, `npm run setup -- --qa` (copies `.env.qa`) and `QA_PORT=3102 npm run qa:server -- --production` in the background.

Both use the same QA workspace, so they see the same data. Each is ready when `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "x-moneo-test: 1" http://localhost:<port>/api/health` prints 401 or 200. Run `npm run qa:auth` if the session is older than an hour.

Set up the data the change needs the way the nearest spec in `e2e/` does, through the app. An empty page measures an empty page.

## 2. Opening the app

`node scripts/perf-pages.mjs 5 before=http://localhost:3102 after=http://localhost:3101`

It loads every main page cold on desktop and mobile, the two builds interleaved run by run so machine noise hits both alike, and prints the medians: TTFB, first paint, LCP, time until the heading shows, layout shift, long tasks and JS KB. The full results are in `.qa/perf-before.json` and `.qa/perf-after.json`.

## 3. What the change touches

Time the action the change affects, from the owner's tap until its result shows: opening a panel, an import, accepting a card, a sync, a chat answer. Use Playwright against both ports, one warm-up and then at least 5 runs each, and take the median.

Mock AI, bank and Scalable with `page.route`, the way `e2e/*.mocked.spec.ts` does, so nothing costs money and the number is Moneo's own time, not the provider's. `scripts/perf-interactions.mjs` makes real AI calls: run it only when the owner asks.

For work with no screen (a workflow step, a `lib/` function), time it with a small script against the QA backend, both checkouts, same runs and median.

## 4. Read the numbers

A slowdown is a median more than 10% **and** more than 50 ms worse, or more JS on a page. Anything smaller is noise; when in doubt, run again.

A slowdown means this change made Moneo slower. Find the cause (a trace with `--trace on`, the Network tab, the React Profiler) and fix it before opening the PR, then measure again. If the extra time cannot be avoided, say in the PR what costs it and why, and ask the owner.

## 5. Hand over

Add this to the PR description:

```markdown
## Speed

Production builds on QA data, median of 5 runs. Before: `<base sha>`. After: `<head sha>`.

| What | Before | After | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Open Home, desktop (heading shows) | 640 ms | 610 ms | −5% |
| Open Home, mobile | 820 ms | 800 ms | −2% |
| Accept a cash card (tap → new balance) | 310 ms | 290 ms | −6% |
```

List Home, every page the change touches and the action from step 3. Put any slowdown first, with its cause.

## 6. Clean up

Stop only the servers you started, found by port and checkout path, never by name. Remove the base worktree with `git worktree remove ../moneo-speed-base`.
